properties.displayName: Azure Data Platform Security - Storage, Event Hub, Event Grid, Data Factory, Functions, SQL DB, Purview, Logic Apps
properties.description: This policy initiative enforces security controls for ADLS Gen2/Azure Storage, Event Hub, Event Grid, Azure Data Factory, Azure Functions, Azure SQL Database, Microsoft Purview, and Logic Apps, including network access restrictions, encryption, identity management, authentication, and diagnostic logging.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the storage account isn't exposed on the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should restrict network access
metadata.description: Network access to storage accounts should be restricted using virtual network rules.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should prevent shared key access
metadata.description: Audit requirement of Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) to authorize requests for your storage account.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
metadata.description: Audit requirement of Secure transfer in your storage account. Secure transfer is an option that forces your storage account to accept requests only from secure connections (HTTPS).

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should have infrastructure encryption
metadata.description: Enable infrastructure encryption for higher level of assurance that the data is secure. When infrastructure encryption is enabled, data in a storage account is encrypted twice.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage account public access should be disallowed
metadata.description: Anonymous public read access to containers and blobs in Azure Storage is a convenient way to share data but might present security risks.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should prevent cross tenant object replication
metadata.description: Audit restriction of object replication for your storage account. By default, users can configure object replication with a source storage account in one Azure AD tenant and a destination account in a different tenant.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should have SAS policies configured
metadata.description: Ensure storage accounts have shared access signature (SAS) expiration policy enabled. Users use a SAS to delegate access to resources in Azure Storage account.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage account keys should not be expired
metadata.description: Ensure the user storage account keys are not expired when key expiration policy is set, for improving security of account keys by taking action when the keys are expired.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should allow access from trusted Microsoft services
metadata.description: Some Microsoft services that interact with storage accounts operate from networks that can't be granted access through network rules. Allow trusted Microsoft services to access the storage account.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure storage accounts to disable public network access
metadata.description: To improve the security of Storage Accounts, ensure that they aren't exposed to the public internet and can only be accessed from a private endpoint.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure secure transfer of data on a storage account
metadata.description: Secure transfer is an option that forces your storage account to accept requests only from secure connections (HTTPS).

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure your Storage account public access to be disallowed
metadata.description: Anonymous public read access to containers and blobs in Azure Storage is a convenient way to share data but might present security risks.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Geo-redundant storage should be enabled for Storage Accounts
metadata.description: Use geo-redundancy to create highly available applications.

metadata.displayName: Effect - [Preview]: Storage Accounts should be Zone Redundant
metadata.description: Storage Accounts can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not. If its redundancy array does not contain 'Zone', it is not zone-redundant.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Modify Azure File Sync to disable public network access
metadata.description: Azure File Sync's internet-accessible public endpoint is disabled by your organizational policy. You may still access the Storage Sync Service via its private endpoint(s).

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage encryption scopes should use double encryption for data at rest
metadata.description: Enable infrastructure encryption for encryption scopes for higher level of assurance that the data is secure.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should be migrated to new Azure Resource Manager resources
metadata.description: Use new Azure Resource Manager for your storage accounts to provide security enhancements.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage accounts should restrict network access using virtual network rules
metadata.description: Protect your storage accounts from potential threats using virtual network rules as a preferred method instead of IP-based filtering.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Encryption for storage services should be enforced
metadata.description: Deny creation of storage accounts where services encryption is not enforced.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Local users should be restricted for Storage Accounts
metadata.description: Deny creation of local users on storage accounts.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Resource Access Rules resource IDs should be restricted
metadata.description: Restrict resource access rules resource IDs on storage accounts.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Resource Access Rules Tenants should be restricted
metadata.description: Restrict resource access rules tenant IDs on storage accounts.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage Accounts should restrict CORS rules
metadata.description: Deny storage accounts that allow CORS rules.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Storage Accounts with SFTP enabled should be denied
metadata.description: Deny storage accounts with SFTP enabled.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Virtual network rules should be restricted for Storage Accounts
metadata.description: Restrict virtual network rules on storage account network ACLs.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Event Hub Namespaces should disable public network access
metadata.description: Event Hub should have public network access disabled.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Event Hub namespaces should use private link
metadata.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Event Hub namespaces should use a customer-managed key for encryption
metadata.description: Azure Event Hubs supports the option of encrypting data at rest with customer-managed keys.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Event Hub namespaces should have double encryption enabled
metadata.description: Enabling double encryption helps protect and safeguard your data to meet your organizational security and compliance commitments.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Hub namespaces should have local authentication methods disabled
metadata.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Event Hub namespaces exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - All authorization rules except RootManageSharedAccessKey should be removed from Event Hub namespace
metadata.description: Event Hub clients should not use a namespace level access policy that provides access to all queues and topics in a namespace. To align with the least privilege security model, you should create access policies at the entity level for queues and topics.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Authorization rules on the Event Hub instance should be defined
metadata.description: Audit existence of authorization rules on Event Hub entities to grant least-privileged access.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Azure Event Hub namespaces to disable local authentication
metadata.description: Disable local authentication methods so that your Azure Event Hub namespaces exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - [Preview]: Event Hubs should be Zone Redundant
metadata.description: Event Hubs can be configured to be Zone Redundant or not.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Event Hub should use a virtual network service endpoint
metadata.description: This policy audits any Event Hub not configured to use a virtual network service endpoint.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid domains should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid domains should have local authentication methods disabled
metadata.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure Event Grid domains exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid domains should use private link
metadata.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid topics should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid topics should have local authentication methods disabled
metadata.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure Event Grid topics exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid topics should use private link
metadata.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid namespaces should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the resource isn't exposed on the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Event Grid partner namespaces should have local authentication methods disabled
metadata.description: Disabling local authentication methods improves security by ensuring that Azure Event Grid partner namespaces exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Azure Event Grid domains to disable local authentication
metadata.description: Disable local authentication methods so that your Event Grid domains exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Azure Event Grid topics to disable local authentication
metadata.description: Disable local authentication methods so that your Event Grid topics exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Event Grid partner namespaces to disable local authentication
metadata.description: Disable local authentication methods so that your Event Grid partner namespaces exclusively require Azure Active Directory identities for authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Modify Event Grid domains to disable public network access
metadata.description: Disable public network access for Azure Event Grid domains resource so that it is not accessible over the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Modify Event Grid topics to disable public network access
metadata.description: Disable public network access for Azure Event Grid topics resource so that it is not accessible over the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Public network access on Azure Data Factory should be disabled
metadata.description: Disabling the public network access property improves security by ensuring your Azure Data Factory can only be accessed from a private endpoint.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Data Factory should use private link
metadata.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure data factories should be encrypted with a customer-managed key
metadata.description: Use customer-managed keys to manage the encryption at rest of your Azure Data Factory.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Data Factory linked services should use Key Vault for storing secrets
metadata.description: To ensure secrets (such as connection strings) are managed securely, require users to provide secrets using an Azure Key Vault instead of specifying them inline in linked services.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Data Factory linked services should use system-assigned managed identity authentication when it is supported
metadata.description: Using system-assigned managed identity when communicating with data stores via linked services avoids the use of less secured credentials such as passwords or connection strings.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Data Factory should use a Git repository for source control
metadata.description: Configure your data factory with Git integration to gain change tracking, collaboration, continuous integration, and deployment capabilities.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Data Factories to disable public network access
metadata.description: Disable public network access for your Data Factory so that it is not accessible over the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - SSIS integration runtimes on Azure Data Factory should be joined to a virtual network
metadata.description: Azure Virtual Network deployment provides enhanced security and isolation for your Azure-SSIS Integration Runtimes on Azure Data Factory.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access improves security by ensuring that the function app isn't exposed on the public internet.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should use managed identity
metadata.description: Use a managed identity for enhanced authentication security.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should only be accessible over HTTPS
metadata.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should use the latest TLS version
metadata.description: Periodically, newer versions are released for TLS either due to security flaws, include additional functionality, and enhance speed. Upgrade to the latest TLS version for Function apps.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should have remote debugging turned off
metadata.description: Remote debugging requires inbound ports to be opened on function apps. Remote debugging should be turned off.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should have resource logs enabled
metadata.description: Audit enabling of resource logs on the app. This enables you to recreate activity trails for investigation purposes if a security incident occurs or your network is compromised.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function apps should not have CORS configured to allow every resource to access your apps
metadata.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) should not allow all domains to access your Function app. Allow only required domains to interact with your Function app.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Function app slots should only be accessible over HTTPS
metadata.description: Use of HTTPS ensures server/service authentication and protects data in transit from network layer eavesdropping attacks.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Public network access on Azure SQL Database should be disabled
metadata.description: Disabling the public network access property improves security by ensuring your Azure SQL Database can only be accessed from a private endpoint.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Private endpoint connections on Azure SQL Database should be enabled
metadata.description: Private endpoint connections enforce secure communication by enabling private connectivity to Azure SQL Database.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Database should be running TLS version 1.2 or newer
metadata.description: Setting TLS version to 1.2 or newer improves security by ensuring your Azure SQL Database can only be accessed from clients using TLS 1.2 or newer.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Database should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled
metadata.description: Require Azure SQL logical servers to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication. This policy doesnt block servers from being created with local authentication enabled.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Transparent Data Encryption on SQL databases should be enabled
metadata.description: Transparent data encryption should be enabled to protect data-at-rest and meet compliance requirements.

metadata.displayName: Effect - SQL servers should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
metadata.description: Implementing Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with your own key provides increased transparency and control over the TDE Protector.

metadata.displayName: Effect - An Azure Active Directory administrator should be provisioned for SQL servers
metadata.description: Audit provisioning of an Azure Active Directory administrator for your SQL server to enable Azure AD authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Defender for SQL should be enabled for unprotected Azure SQL servers
metadata.description: Audit Azure SQL servers without Advanced Data Security.

metadata.displayName: Effect - SQL databases should have vulnerability findings resolved
metadata.description: Monitor vulnerability assessment scan results and recommendations for how to remediate database vulnerabilities.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Vulnerability assessment should be enabled on your SQL servers
metadata.description: Audit Azure SQL servers which do not have recurring vulnerability assessment scans enabled.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Azure SQL Server to disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling the public network access property shuts down public connectivity such that Azure SQL Server can only be accessed from a private endpoint.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Deploy SQL DB transparent data encryption
metadata.description: Enable transparent data encryption on SQL databases.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Managed Instances should disable public network access
metadata.description: Disabling public network access (public endpoint) on Azure SQL Managed Instances improves security by ensuring that it can only be accessed from inside their virtual networks or via Private Endpoints.

metadata.displayName: Effect - SQL managed instances should use customer-managed keys to encrypt data at rest
metadata.description: Implementing Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with your own key provides you with increased transparency and control over the TDE Protector.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Long-term geo-redundant backup should be enabled for Azure SQL Databases
metadata.description: This policy audits any Azure SQL Database with long-term geo-redundant backup not enabled.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Database should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled during creation
metadata.description: Require Azure SQL logical servers to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Managed Instance should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled
metadata.description: Require Azure SQL Managed Instance to use Microsoft Entra-only authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure SQL Managed Instance should have Microsoft Entra-only authentication enabled during creation
metadata.description: Require Azure SQL Managed Instance to be created with Microsoft Entra-only authentication.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Configure Azure Defender to be enabled on SQL managed instances
metadata.description: Enable Azure Defender on your Azure SQL Managed Instances to detect anomalous activities indicating unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit databases.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Azure Purview should use private endpoints
metadata.description: Azure Private Link lets you connect your virtual network to Azure services without a public IP address at the source or destination. The Private Link platform handles the connectivity between the consumer and services over the Azure backbone network. By mapping private endpoints to your Azure Purview account, data leakage risks are reduced.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Logic Apps should be deployed into Integration Service Environment
metadata.description: Deploying Logic Apps into Integration Service Environment in a virtual network unlocks Logic Apps networking and security features and provides you with greater control over your network configuration.

metadata.displayName: Effect - Logic Apps Integration Service Environment should be encrypted with customer-managed keys
metadata.description: Deploy into Integration Service Environment to manage encryption at rest of Logic Apps data using customer-managed keys.
